column1: # ZAP rules for the operator console scans (tests/dast/run_zap.sh).
# rule id<TAB>FAIL|WARN|IGNORE<TAB>(rule name) and, for IGNORE, the reason.
# FAIL fails the job. WARN is reported only. IGNORE hides a passive alert and keeps an
# active rule from running. Alerts of Informational risk never fail the job, whatever the
# level. The image pins ZAP itself; the scan scripts update and install the beta rule
# add-ons at start, and a rule missing from this file is treated as WARN.

column3: (Cookie Without Secure Flag) loopback is plain HTTP; under the HTTPS external name the cookie is Secure
(Information Disclosure - Sensitive Information in HTTP Referrer Header)
(Information Disclosure - Suspicious Comments) flags words such as 'user' and 'select' in the console's public, commented source
(Heartbleed OpenSSL Vulnerability (Indicative)) plain HTTP on loopback; there is no TLS to test
(Strict-Transport-Security Header) loopback is plain HTTP; HSTS is sent under the HTTPS external name

(HTTP to HTTPS Insecure Transition in Form Post)
(HTTPS to HTTP Insecure Transition in Form Post)
(Content Cacheability) informational: Cache-Control no-store on every response is deliberate
(Modern Web Application) informational: says the console is a JavaScript application
(Authentication Request Identified) informational: marks a request ZAP takes for a sign-in
(Session Management Response Identified) informational: marks a response ZAP takes for session management
(Verification Request Identified) informational: marks a request ZAP takes for verification
(ZAP is Out of Date) ZAP itself is pinned by image digest and updated on purpose
(Server Side Technology Version with Known Vulnerabilities)
(Stats Passive Scan Rule) collects scan statistics, raises no alerts
(Source Code Disclosure - File Inclusion) reads the API refusing "/" in a query value (400) as file inclusion; the console reads no file named by a request
(HTTPS Content Available via HTTP) there is no HTTPS listener on loopback to compare with
(HTTP Only Site) the console serves plain HTTP on loopback by design; HTTPS comes from a proxy under external_host
(Heartbleed OpenSSL Vulnerability) plain HTTP on loopback; there is no TLS to test
